question.text: Mr. Karan Mehta is studying buy-out variants. He reads that a particular structure 'emerges from the MBO when certain elements are missing from the incumbent management team and therefore have to be sourced from outside'. Which buy-out variant is this?

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 8.3.1.3 defines MBI as a variant of MBO where the management team is assembled from OUTSIDE to do the buyout, typically because the incumbent team lacks certain skills. Pure MBO with a fully external team is rare. The Trap: Option A describes a financing structure, not a management sourcing structure. Option B is the parent concept — MBI is the variant with external team. Option D refers to exit to another buyout fund, not team sourcing. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C is the exam that explicitly tests MBI/MBO/LBO taxonomy. Distributor exams only refer to 'buyouts' generically. Manager's Pro-Tip: In an MBI, vest the external CEO's equity over 4 years with performance milestones — you are betting on untested execution chemistry with the existing mid-management.
